Subject: Concordant SDK bridge & telemetry pilot

Hi Elena,

Great meeting earlier — thanks for the time. As discussed, Concordant's query layer and prompt orchestration are a really nice fit for a joint pilot that demonstrates seamless SDK-level integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex customers and end-to-end telemetry (token-level cost, trace spans, and prompt/regeneration events).

Proposed high-level pilot goals:
- Build a Redwood adapter plugin that Concordant can drop into existing LangChain / LlamaIndex stacks (Python + Node) so their customers can route inference to Redwood Dedicated or Hosted variants.
- Add tracing hooks so a single trace id travels from Concordant's orchestration -> Redwood runtime; expose span timings and token counts in the trace.
- Surface prompt-level quality metrics and a small regression test suite (5–10 prompt templates) to validate output parity across model variants.
- Deliver a short SOW and a staging run with one internal Concordant dev team + Redwood eng support.

Do you have capacity to start a 4–6 week POC? If yes, can you share: team contacts (engineering + infra), a staging AWS account or temporary credentials, and any constraints around telemetry (PII, sampling, retention)? I attached a one‑page pilot outline to make it easier to share internally.

If that sounds good I’ll loop in our ISV integrations lead and runtime engineer to draft an implementation checklist.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Hi all — thanks Vanessa. Below is an integration checklist / proposed acceptance criteria I use for LangChain/LlamaIndex ISV adapters. I’ve kept it pragmatic (goal: install & run in a day for your staging team).

Adapter checklist (minimum viable):
1) SDK surface
   - Provide a lightweight Redwood transport for LangChain (Base LLM class) and a LlamaIndex connector.
   - Offer both synchronous and streaming responses.
2) Auth & routing
   - Support API key + optional client certificate for Dedicated routing.
   - Config knobs to pin model_variant and fallback model.
3) Tracing / telemetry
   - Accept incoming trace id header (X-Trace-Id) and emit trace spans to Redwood tracing backend.
   - Include tokens_requested, tokens_generated, model_variant, and prompt_template_id in span metadata.
   - Sampling default: 1% (configurable) with immediate on-error sampling.
4) Prompt provenance
   - Adapter attaches prompt_template_id and template_version as request metadata.
5) QA / regression
   - Run 8 canonical prompts against three model variants (fast/standard/precise) and compare for gross regressions on a small metric set.
6) Security & compliance
   - No customer PII is persisted by default. Ensure retention config documented.
7) Docs & example
   - Example repo with install + small demo notebook and a short runbook for staging.

Deliverables and timeline (tentative):
- Week 0: discovery + staging access
- Week 1–2: adapter prototype (LangChain Python) + example notebook
- Week 3: tracing integration & telemetry schema (small JSON schema)
- Week 4: regression tests, docs, and joint demo

Links / artifacts:
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEFgHIjKlmnOPqRstUv (adapter spec + prompt set)
- DocuSign SOW: https://www.docusign.com/contract/ABCDEF123456

I attached an adapter interface spec and a CSV with the initial prompt suite. I’ll prepare a short runbook for the Concordant devs to install the adapter in staging.

Thanks — Marissa

Quick engineering notes from runtime:
- Trace propagation: we will honor X-Trace-Id (string up to 128 chars). If missing, runtime will generate a trace id and return it in the response header.
- Spans & metrics: accepted metadata keys: prompt_template_id, template_version, client_request_id, model_variant, tokens_requested, tokens_generated. We can surface token-level timing in spans but recommend sampling to reduce cost.
- Model variants: confirm expected sequence length and average prompt size. Long sequences ( > 4k tokens) require a different kernel path; call this out up front.
- Auth: for staging use short-lived API keys (we'll provide a staging role). For Dedicated tests we can collaborate on mTLS later.
- Staging creds: we need an IAM user/email to add to our staging account. Ideally an IAM role with limited access to create minimal infra (S3 for logs, temp bucket for artifacts).

Estimate: ~2.5 engineer-weeks (Marissa and I split work) to delivery prototype + basic tracing. If Concordant wants Node adapter in parallel add ~1 week.

I’ll sketch the runtime config snippets and a sample span JSON after we confirm the staging details.

— Jonas
